#491. eharmony app reviews: Subscribers share whether it’s worth it

It's incredible that eharmony has managed to stay relevant in the online dating world. The dating site launched back at the turn of the millennium and held firm by focusing on a more substantive, personality-based approach to online matchmaking. It's not perfect, of course, and different daters prefer different approaches to finding partners.

While eharmony members generally appreciate the depth of its matchmaking algorithm, they sometimes complain about the cost and the number of fake profiles, particularly since artificial intelligence has become more widely available.

Here's what real eharmony users had to say about the site, from the best features to the worst experiences:

AdultFriendFinder — readers’ pick for casual connections

Tinder — top pick for fast hookups

Hinge — popular choice for regular meetups

Pure — best for anonymous hookups

OkCupid — best app for inclusivity

If you're looking for some genuine substance on dating sites, you often have to filter out all the people who are only in it for short-term fun. At least, that's the case on other dating platforms. But eharmony largely bypasses that problem, first through its reputation (fun fact: it began as a Christian dating site!) and through its detailed sign-up process, which includes completing the eharmony compatibility questionnaire.

Reddit reviewers have consistently lauded this focus on substance in the screening process ("it forces you to focus on depth over pure visuals") and found the compatibility scores, assigned based on your answers to the personality quiz you take when you sign up, to be a useful way of evaluating matches before starting a conversation.

Here's a story from one older gentleman: "My mindset was that I really needed to be fully honest in my answers, because why would I pay for a service and not be honest? After a few days, I got my matches. A day later, I got a nice message from a woman 10 years younger than me. We exchanged some messages, and then I looked at our match score after she prompted me about it. We were 126 out of 140. I decided to go with it because she and I were really vibing on each other. A year later we got engaged and will marry next year."

For reference, a compatibility score of 126 on eharmony is incredibly rare. As one Redditor responded, "When I was on there, I never had greater than 105 with any match."

A common complaint over the years about eharmony has been the cost of the premium membership, which you need to sign up for to get the most out of the site (eharmony doesn't even let you see photos without upgrading to its premium service). There are three premium membership tiers to choose from (Light, Plus, and Unlimited), with pricing varying somewhat by your location, but you should expect to pay at least $15 per month for a membership, which makes it more expensive than a standard Netflix subscription but around the same price as a cheap gym membership.

Users have complained about both the price and the cancellation process: "I’ve tried eHarmony and found it way too expensive for what it offers, and to top it [off], the process of cancellation is so complicated," said one Reddit reviewer. Other users were unhappy with its automatic membership renewals or the difficulty of canceling a subscription, even just 12 hours after signing up.

That said, eharmony entices users with steep discounts — sometimes up to 50 percent off the regular membership price — so if you keep tabs on offers, you can sign up and get substantial savings.

It's a fact of online dating: different sites are built for different demographics. That means certain age groups gravitate towards certain sites. You'll already know that if you've ever used Tinder as a middle-aged adult.

Older daters, divorced daters, and anyone looking for a more mature partner should definitely try eharmony. We named it the "gold standard" for daters over 40 for a reason — the older age bracket is eharmony's wheelhouse.

Here's a typical experience from an older male dater: "45 yo divorced guy here. I signed up with eHarmony and Bumble 2 months ago based on recommendations from co-workers. I've had much better luck with eHarmony than Bumble. My highest compatibility ratings are in the 110 to 116 range, and these comprise about 33 percent of my daily feed. The other 33 percent are in the 100 to 105 rating scale, and the final 33 percent are in the 89 to 99 rating scale. [...] In contrast, I have connected with zero women on Bumble Premium after 2 months."

In the age of AI and cheaply produced deepfakes, dating sites have been swamped by fake profiles. Indeed, eharmony users have found themselves sifting through numerous fake dating profiles before finding a real human being to engage. It's frustrating.

One of the top-rated posts on the /r/eharmony subreddit in the last year decries, "The fake profile problem has got noticeably worse," complaining that of the 14 likes their account received, 11 came from obviously fake accounts.

But how big a problem is this, really? For older daters unaccustomed to filtering out fake profiles and photos, it can be a major pain in the butt, sure. But if you're even remotely internet-savvy, you shouldn't have too much trouble distinguishing between real and fake users. And you're guarantee you'll encounter this problem on pretty much every dating platform — so don't let it put you off using eharmony. And because eharmony has tight restrictions for free members, you can largely side-step the fake profile issue if you upgrade to a paid subscription. This allows you to only interact with other paying members, which effectively eliminates those annoying bots.

#489. $1,200 Off the iPhone Duo? Here’s How Carrier Deals Actually Work

Don’t expect Apple to offer a sale on the iPhone Duo. The company almost never discounts its products, especially new ones that are selling like hotcakes. (It’s back-ordered.) With the Duo starting at $2,000, it’s very expensive for most people to buy Apple’s first foldable, and the best way to get a deal may be through a carrier.

Of course, there are stipulations, but if you qualify, you could “save” significantly on an iPhone Duo—as much as $1,200, knocking the price to $800. (Keep reading, there’s a catch.) Here are some of the potential deals we found.

Shipping times are stretching into January, so it may be a while before you can get your hands on an iPhone Duo, even with one of these offers.

If you sign up for an Experience Beyond plan, T-Mobile will credit you $1,200. To qualify, you need to purchase the iPhone Duo and sign up for the Experience Beyond 2.0 plan for 36 months if you’re a new customer, or sign up for the Experience Beyond 2.0, Experience Beyond, or Go5G Next plans if you’re an existing T-Mobile customer and not already enrolled in another payment plan.

You don’t get $1,200 upfront. Instead, T-Mobile spreads that amount across 36 monthly credits on your bill. For the 256-GB base model, for example, you’ll pay $22.22 a month for the phone on top of the monthly plan; those payments total about $800 over three years, plus the Experience Beyond 2.0 plan is $100 a month, excluding taxes and fees. The deal doesn’t apply when you pay in full or choose a cheaper plan. If you hate expensive contracts, this isn’t for you.

T-Mobile offers several other incentives for the iPhone Duo, including $1,200 off with trade-in or $1,000 off for seniors, military personnel, students, and first responders. To see what you might qualify for, click on the “see promotions” link on the T-Mobile iPhone Duo purchase page.

If you’re not clamoring for the iPhone Duo, T-Mobile’s incentives also apply to the new iPhone 18 Pro and other models.

AT&T and Verizon are also offering incentives on the iPhone Duo. AT&T has a trade-in plan similar to T-Mobile’s: You’ll pay $22.23 a month for the phone for 36 months, which is equivalent to $1,200 off after you’ve fulfilled your contract. AT&T also has a “contract-breaking” deal that will get you an $800 reward card when you switch to AT&T, but you’d still have to pay the full price of the iPhone Duo.

The same goes for Verizon. You can get $1,200 off a 36-month Unlimited Ultimate plan, with or without a trade-in, as a new or existing customer. As an extra incentive, Verizon is including your choice of an Apple Watch Series 12 or iPad.

Whichever company’s deal you pursue, you’re entering into what is essentially a contract. The phone will also be locked to the carrier until you’ve made your final payment. You’ll also pay more after fees and taxes are added, although there’s no monthly interest. When you factor everything—the cost of a particular plan and the discounted phone—it could be what you're currently paying for a premium plan, or possibly much more.

We usually don’t recommend cell phone contracts; it’s best to get a phone unlocked, even if it means paying full price. However, if you plan to stay with a carrier long-term and want to lower the cost of the iPhone Duo, it’s still worth considering. But do the math before committing.

#488. LA communities kick out Big Oil

After years of advocacy from residents and legal battles with Big Oil, Los Angeles voted to ban drilling and phase out oil extraction in the city. It's the first city in the United States to kick the oil industry out.

Los Angeles has become the largest city in the US to ban oil drilling, after years of lawsuits and campaigning by residents who raised the alarm over pollution and potential health risks from nearby wells .

"Front-line communities have pushed the city for a solution for this for over a decade," said local resident Wendy Miranda, who has campaigned for years with STAND-LA, a coalition of community groups working to end neighborhood oil drilling.

The ordinance, approved by the LA City Council on October 28, puts an immediate stop to oil extraction and bans the redrilling or deepening of wells. Existing operations must be phased out within city limits over the next 20 years.

Though LA City is only part of greater Los Angeles, the move affects hundreds of active wells and thousands of inactive ones, many located in working class communities of color.

"In South LA, working-class families have had corporations drilling across the street from their homes," said council president Marqueece Harris-Dawson in a statement. "No one should have to live near an oil drilling site."

Rock Zierman, CEO of the California Independent Petroleum Association (CIPA), told DW, "CIPA believes this ordinance constitutes an unlawful taking of private property."

LA follows much smaller Culver City, also in California, in moving against urban oil production, and begins the process of ending its long, complex relationship with fossil fuels.

California's oil industry expanded rapidly in the early 20th century, when the state produced roughly a quarter of the world's oil. Lots of that so-called black gold was around LA and as the city grew, homes, schools and businesses were built around existing oil infrastructure.

Today, wells can be found beneath residential areas, close to playgrounds, along the coast and in some of the city's most densely populated and largely working-class neighborhoods. Some have been permanently sealed or plugged for decades, while others remain active or are idle.

Under California law, an idle well is one that has not produced oil for two years. Unlike plugged wells, they can potentially return to production.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Residents living near the active and inactive wells report strong odors, headaches, nausea and breathing difficulties. Another concern is air quality. Oil wells can release toxic pollutants, including benzene and hydrogen sulfide, and research has linked proximity to oil extraction with higher rates of respiratory illness and reduced lung function.

But both active and idle wells can also leak methane — a potent greenhouse gas that contributes to climate change — while residents say occasional accidents or breakages send oil flowing down city streets.

"Frontline communities have been experiencing or have experienced for decades living near these toxic sites and having to pay for that with their health," said Miranda, a policy director with Esperanza Community Housing, a nonprofit providing affordable housing services.

Miranda told DW she and her mother both have asthma. The council vote "definitely represents hope," she added.

LA City Council initially approved an ordinance to phase out oil extraction back in 2022 after successful lobbying by residents like Wendy Miranda. But oil companies challenged the measure in court, with industry groups successfully arguing that the city lacked the legal authority to impose the ban.

California subsequently passed legislation giving local governments greater power to regulate and restrict oil and gas operations, putting the possibility of a phaseout back on the table.

In an emailed statement to DW, CIPA CEO Rock Zierman said energy companies were prepared to challenge the new ordinance.

Zierman added that it would make city residents more dependent on foreign oil from countries with lower environmental standards when they are "already struggling" with high gas prices.

"It sends the jobs, investment and revenue elsewhere while leaving Californians to pay the bill," said Zierman.

The relationship between local oil production and prices at the pump is not straightforward and is influenced by a number of factors, according to the California Energy Commission, the state's main energy policy agency. Those include the cost of crude oil, refining, transportation, distribution and local taxes.

Even though the US is the world's largest oil producer, it exports and imports crude oil, as well as refined petroleum products. Because oil is traded globally, US residents are exposed to the same price fluctuations as people elsewhere, no matter how much of the fossil fuel is produced domestically.

California's oil industry and the amount of oil it produces have been steadily declining since the 1980s. In the coastal lowlands known as the LA Basin, output is 43% lower than eight years ago, with the amount of oil extracted falling more rapidly than the number of open wells.

When wells stop producing, it is up to the oil operators to remove equipment and plug them. The state agency that regulates oil and gas, CalGEM, and the LA fire department oversee plugging operations, and also seal wells for which no-one takes responsibility.

But many have not yet been plugged — some 80% of idle wells in LA have been inactive for more than eight years, and about a third for over a century.

The cost of plugging a well also varies widely, with estimates ranging from hundreds of thousands to millions of dollars. California law requires operators to submit plugging plans or face annual fines that increase with the amount of time the well has been idle.

But those fines aren't always paid. According to CalGEM's own data, the agency collected just $1 million out of $36 million (€32 million) in fines in 2025.

A report by Carbon Tracker also found that if all future profits from oil companies operating in California went to decommissioning wells, the state would still face a shortfall of $7 billion. The cost would by default fall to taxpayers, according to Carbon Tracker.

Miranda told DW that the next step for community activists is to reduce the 20-year timeline and have the oil sector "pay for this cleanup."  For now, she is says both she and her mother are hopeful that future generations "can have better health and breathe cleaner air."

#487. The 93 best Christmas gifts for 2026: Our favorite gift ideas from Apple, Lego, Kindle, and brands youve never heard of

Ready or not, the holiday shopping season is underway. Choosing the best Christmas gifts for the ones you love is either an epic quest that you look forward to every year — or one you dread. Luckily, we spend our days testing all the latest gadgets, trending products, and gift-worthy gear, and we know exactly what to recommend.

For 2026, our Christmas wishlist is simple: it's all the awesome stuff we loved most this year, including the products we named Mashable Gift of the Year winners. That includes the newest gadgets, the swoonworthy items we just had to buy for ourselves, and some classic all-time Mashable favorites. With input from our own tech reporters, shopping editors, and product reviewers, every single Christmas gift idea we recommend is an item we use, love, or have given to others ourselves.

Whether you're searching for the best Christmas gifts for mom and dad, your sweetheart, cool teens, or stocking stuffers everyone will love, start with our Christmas gift guide. So, join us as we put on our Santa hats and share the very best Christmas gift ideas of the year.

Several Mashable reporters dramatically curbed their screen time with the help of the Brick, a pocket-sized gadget that locks certain apps on your phone. That physical element makes it way more effective than traditional screen-time apps. "My favorite use of Bricking my phone is before bed, as it ensures social media isn't the first thing I see when I wake up," said lead shopping reporter Samantha Mangino. Throw in a cute Brick Case while you're at it, too. Read our full review of the Brick.

Charging devices are always some of the best practical gifts and stocking stuffers. Anker has an endless number of high-powered charging solutions, but we’re especially fond of two. First, the ultra-thin Nano MagSafe Power Bank attaches magnetically to compatible phones for convenient wireless charging. Then, there’s the Nano Smart Display Charger, which can fast-charge smartphones and let you know when it's done with a built-in smart display.

Wired earbuds are back in style, and Apple's EarPods — the white 'buds that used to come with old iPhones — are a classic, affordable option. Senior shopping reporter Haley Henschel replaced her uncomfortable AirPods Pro 2 with them and never looked back. "Join me on the wired side," she wrote. "The sound quality is good enough [and] the cover charge is cheap."

The Kodak Charmera is a miniature camera that comes in a blind box (like a Labubu), so you don't know exactly which color you're going to get. The best part is that it can actually take photos and videos — it's not just a decorative toy — and its shots are delightfully nostalgic. Multiple Mashable staffers have one of these hanging on their keychains or purses' hardware.

The Nothing Ear (3a) are an excellent AirPods Pro alternative and some of the best budget earbuds available. They sound as good as they look, delivering clear, bold audio in a transparent design. Call quality is their biggest strength, rivaling earbuds that cost nearly three times as much.

These rechargeable electric hand warmers come personally recommended by Mashable tech editor Timothy Beck Werth, who's been slipping them into Christmas stockings for years. They have a cute design and built-in flashlight, but most importantly, they keep your hands and fingers nice and toasty even in the bitter cold. If you're looking for gifts under $25 for a White Elephant or Secret Santa gift exchange, we promise these will be popular.

A Welly first-aid kit is another of our go-to stocking stuffers. The brand is best known for its adorable, kid-friendly Bravery Bandages with fun designs, but even adults will appreciate this colorful and travel-friendly med kit, which has all the essentials you need to treat little bumps, scrapes, burns, and ouchies. Pack one in your dopp kit when you travel, or keep it in your medicine cabinet year-round.

Amazon just dropped some iPad alternatives for Android users with tighter budgets: the new Alexa tablets. Their premium aluminum chassis are sleek and colorful, and the Alexa+ AI assistant is built right into them. Plus, unlike Amazon's older Fire tablets, they have full access to the Google Play Store. If your gifting budget has no bounds, we think the high-end Alexa Tablet 12 Pro with an optional "nanomatte" display is one of the best Christmas gift ideas for digital artists.

The Ambient Dreamie is a new smart alarm clock that "makes it easy to pretend like your phone doesn't exist," Henschel wrote. "It doesn't require an app for setup, and it eliminates most excuses for bringing your phone to bed by offloading your alarms, night lighting, and sleep content." She said it helped her fall asleep faster and wake up easier. This fall, the Dreamie added a podcast feature, and contactless sleep tracking is next on the docket. Read our full review of the Ambient Dreamie.

Apple finally revisited its HomePod mini smart speaker this fall to give it a faster processor and a new "Sound Glow" feature that can sync with your music. A future software update will add support for the company's Siri AI assistant; if you link it to your phone or iPad, it'll be able to recognize your voice and compete tasks for you using your calendar, texts, and emails. Crucially, it also now comes in pink and green.

This spring, Apple dropped a budget bombshell in the MacBook Neo, a colorful laptop that doesn't look or feel as cheap as it really is. (It starts at just $699.) "Most cheap Windows laptops and Chromebooks have plastic components, but this little guy has the same luxe, all-aluminum build quality as any other MacBook," Henschel wrote, adding that its A18 Pro chip is "extremely impressive" in basic computing scenarios. It's a Mashable Choice Award winner, and we think it's the best laptop for kids and younger students. Read our full review of the Apple MacBook Neo.

Shopping for someone who runs every decision past ChatGPT? We've got just the thing. We’re talking about Pocket, a voice recorder that hides discreetly in any pocket. Moreover, this is a personal AI assistant programmed to take notes, transcribe meetings, and summarize calls. Pocket does a terrific job of extracting key info and providing visual maps of conversations. It's also a great gift idea for college students.

Another Mashable Choice titleholder, the new Oura Ring 5 has a slimmer design that makes it more comfortable to wear for long periods of time — yet it still lasts up to seven days per charge. According to Mangino, who's used to wearing an Apple Watch, its jewelry-like look and fit make it the ultimate everyday wearable. Its "exceptional" activity tracking (her words) and useful health insights are just the icing on the cake. Read our full review of the Oura Ring 5.

Pokémon fever is running high for the legendary franchise's 30th anniversary. So, whether you're shopping for a 5-year-old or a nostalgic millennial who’s still a kid at heart, expect Pokémon gifts to be in very high demand for Christmas 2026.

Select brands have collaborated with the IP to release various special-edition products, including Adidas and Beats. We're also huge fans of the adorable Lego Smart Play Pokémon sets. Our advice: grab available items ASAP or bookmark product pages to watch for restocks. You can thank us later.

We also love the new reMarkable Paper Pure, a powerhouse e-ink writing tablet that doubles as an e-reader for PDF and ePub files, without any ads or pop-ups. Read more about the best e-readers.

(Every size is usually on sale for well under $1,000 — even the huge 85-incher.) It's primo "for casual home theater purposes," Stodart wrote. Read our full review of the TCL QM6K.

Birdbuddy's smart feeders are super popular Christmas gifts, and the brand just came out with two new models: the Birdbuddy Nook and Birdbuddy Home. Parents can use it for FaceTime calls, sending messages, listening to music, catching up on shows, and answering questions or controlling other smart home devices via Siri AI. It also doubles as a digital picture frame. (Like Amazon's Echo Show devices, it's basically an all-in-one hub.) Up to six people can set up their own profiles on it, so it's well-suited for bigger households.

If your family is spread out in different states, then a digital picture frame lets mom, dad, or your grandparents keep track of the entire family — no matter where they are. Everyone in the family can add new pictures remotely, and their picture frames will show a slideshow of your latest adventures.

Classic board games stir up sweet family memories. WS Games leans into that with its vintage-inspired collection. Battleship, Candy Land, Clue, Monopoly, Risk, Scrabble, and numerous other classics receive a bookshelf-worthy makeover. Each edition has a hardcover-style design and interior storage for the pieces, so it can sit proudly on a bookshelf instead of being tucked away in a closet.

What are the best Christmas gifts for men, you might be wondering? We have a whole separate list of gift ideas for guys, but to make things quick, Breeo's USA-made fire pits rock.

Read our full review of the Eufy Robot Vacuum C28.

It's such a good game that a lot of people upgraded to the Nintendo Switch 2 just to play it. Read Mashable's full review of Pokémon Pokopia.

Perry also loved its new magnetic Joy-Con 2s, which are bigger and more satisfying to use than the original Switch's controllers. We think it's the best handheld gaming console to buy in 2026, even after a price hike. Read our full review of the Nintendo Switch 2.

Lego had retro gamers tweaking last year with its awesome Game Boy replica. One look is enough to bring back 32-bit-era memories.

The sixth installment in Sarah J. Maas' hit romantasy series, A Court of Thorns and Roses, arrived this October, and no self-respecting BookTok member should miss it. Both are available in hardcover, paperback, audiobook, and Kindle e-book formats.

"What truly makes it stand out is just how lightweight it is," she wrote — at six inches and half a pound, it's excellent for travel. Read our full review of the new Amazon Kindle.

However, if you have a little more wiggle room in your gifting budget, Mangino thinks the new Kindle Paperwhite Signature Edition is the best Kindle overall: It's waterproof, longer-lasting, and equipped with an adjustable warm light. Read our full review of the Kindle Paperwhite Signature Edition.

Psst: Don't forget to remove the Kindle lockscreen ads before you gift. To quote our tech editor, "it's borderline rude" not to.

Amazon's first page turner, the Kindle Click, "will level up your cozy evenings spent reading," said Mangino, and it's a must-have for the BookTok set. It lets you turn the pages of a Kindle or adjust its brightness when you're snug under the covers of your fuzziest blanket. (It's compatible with models from 2024 onward.) Unlike other page-turners we've tried, it works via Bluetooth. Read our full review of the Amazon Kindle Click. The best tech deal this week The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile

The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile

A gooseneck stand is a "luxury" for any regular e-reader user because it situates the device "within reading distance without any arm fatigue," Mangino said. Based on her testing, this Magipea model works nicely with both Kindle and Kobo models.

Trivia night at the local bar is fun, but hosting one at home can be even better. Hitster is an icebreaker that gets everyone working together to identify hit songs from the past century. Scan a card to play a track, then guess the year it was released. Themed editions — including All American, Guilty Pleasures, and Latino —broaden playability and let you tailor the music to your company.

Multiple Mashable editors and writers swear by Loop's earplugs, which look like jewelry, fit comfortably in most people's ears, and make a unique stocking stuffer. The Loop Experience 2 are great for regular concert- and music festival-goers; Mashable's Henschel even wore them to a Beyoncé show. "I could hear Beyoncé and her band perfectly, but the din of the stadium was almost completely suppressed," she wrote. They come in a range of color options, including some limited-edition metallic variants designed in partnership with Harry Styles.

This spring, Sony launched some new Bluetooth record players for the first time in seven years. Henschel tried the entry-level PS-LX3BT model and called it "a stylish turntable with idiot-proof plug-and-play functionality." She pointed out that it has a USB-B port in the back, which you can use to rip vinyl tracks onto a laptop. If your partner collects vinyl, this is one of those Christmas gift ideas they'll appreciate for years to come. Read our full review of the Sony PS-LX3BT.

CDs are the latest retro tech to have a resurgence among Gen Z. Tracking down a cool old CD player on eBay will earn you a lot of cred, but if you don't want to go through the trouble, this see-through model from Retradisc looks really, really cool. It works with wired or wireless headphones, and best of all, it doesn't cost as much as Sony's new gold-plated Walkman.

Technics continues to make a strong impression in the wireless audio market. When it comes to hi-fi headphones, the new EAH-A1000 are a sonic stunner that put many category leaders to shame. They crush the AirPods Max 2 in most areas and rival the Sony WH-1000XM6 sound quality, while also outlasting both competitors in playtime (up to 45 hours per charge) and multi-point pairing. Plus, the elegant craftsmanship is a 10/10. Every audiophile should have this at the top of their wish list this year.

Choosing a signature scent for your hubby isn’t as easy as picking out a video game; you need to know their olfactory preferences. If you’re unsure what they like — or shopping for someone especially particular — let them decide with one of Fulton & Roark’s discovery sets. The variety gives them a chance to explore different scents and narrow down their next go-to fragrance. (Pro tip: We like Palmetto and Ghost Trees.)

Harry’s has something for every man’s mug. Guys who prefer a clean-shaven look can reach for the brand’s shaving kit, which includes the popular Truman handle with secure grip and multiple five-blade cartridges that deliver close shaves. No-shave November devotees can keep their mane well-kempt with the beard wash and conditioning spray bundle.

Every well-groomed gentleman deserves a luxury electric shaver in his life. The Panasonic Arc5 Pro is our pick for its comfortable, close shaves and flexible head, which is designed to improve cutting performance. It works for both wet and dry shaving, and the built-in pop-up trimmer provides seamless control and navigation to clean up edges around the neckline.

We think the Mashable Choice Award-winning Shark CryoGlow is the best red light mask you can buy right now (and one of the best Christmas gifts for women). It provides more complete coverage than other masks from brands like OmniLux or CurrentBody, and each bulb can emit red, blue, or near-infrared light.

Former senior shopping reporter Leah Stodart was convinced that the CryoGlow’s bacteria-killing blue light setting is what finally cleared a year’s worth of her relentless adult acne. Some cooling under-eye pads complete this luxurious self-care device. Read our full review of the Shark CryoGlow.

Several Mashable staffers use Shark's FlexStyle multi-styler on a regular basis. (Mangino did her wedding hair with it!) It costs half as much as Dyson's iconic Airwrap but works just as well, if not better. It supports a ton of different attachments and has a unique twisting base that functions like a regular hair dryer on its own. Read our full review of the Shark FlexStyle.

The Playground is a cubic gaming console designed for playing family-friendly games with motion controls — no need for a traditional gamepad. Perry described it as "a spiritual successor to the old Xbox Kinect." If this is the first time you're hearing of it, get with the program: It managed to outsell the PlayStation 5 on Black Friday 2025, and was difficult to find in stock during the holiday season last year. If you plan on gifting it within the coming weeks, we'd recommend adding it to your cart ASAP.

Fascinatingly, this squishy little toy is one of the hottest products of 2026. People have stormed stores and waited hours in line to buy them, and there's even a reselling market for them. Mashable's Mangino bought some before the hype and said they "quickly became coveted fidgets among our friends for their pleasing, pliable feel."

Like wired earbuds, CD players, and other items from your childhood, Pokémon cards are so incredibly back — and dare we say, bigger than ever. The Pokémon TCG: 30th Celebration Elite Trainer Box is a giftable bundle that includes 9 booster packs and plenty of other goodies. Amazon is also selling it on an invite-only basis; try your luck because it's well under market price, as of this writing.

Routine can give children structure and help them feel more secure. The Skylight Buddy guides kids through mornings, afternoons, and bedtime, while helping them develop healthy habits and independence. They can add and check off chores, events, and tasks. This digital calendar also functions as an alarm clock and nightlight, signaling wake-up and sleep times. Personalization features help families reinforce goals and daily commitments.

We recently named the Toniebox 2 one of Mashable's Gifts of the Year in our guide to the top gifts for kids. The kid-famous Toniebox is a favorite of the moms and dads on the Mashable team. Whether you're shopping for your own child or trying to earn a reputation as the cool aunt or uncle, kids and parents alike love these screen-free storytelling devices.

If your tyke already has a Toniebox, they can always use more Tonies — the little figures you put on top of the device to activate a new storytime. Bluey and Pokémon Tonies joined the party this year.

Another Mashable Gift of the Year winner, this portable screen-free audio player is a hit with the two kiddos of Nicole Cammorata, Mashable's director of special projects. "Compatible cards power up everything from chapter books and shorter stories to music and learning-based content," she wrote. For an incredibly sweet personalized gift, you can have grandparents, siblings, or friends record custom audio messages on blank Yoto cards.

Gifting a pair of the best Beats headphones is a sure bet for any fashion-forward music lover. Fans of over-ear headphones will appreciate the modular Beats 360, which features a customizable design with swappable ear cushions, IPX4 sweat resistance, pleasant sound, and strong ANC. True wireless conformists can utilize the sporty Powerbeats Pro 2 for exercise and leisure; the revamped earhook design is optimized for comfort and sound performance.

Looking for the best gifts under $100? The Camp Snap 2 is one of our top picks. This screenless digital camera has six built-in filters and super simple controls. To transfer its photos to your phone, all you need is a USB-C cable. Mangino brought a Camp Snap 2 on her Grecian honeymoon this past summer, "and now I have the sweetest photos to look back on," she said. Read our full review of the Camp Snap 2.

The merchandising gods are working their magic this holiday season in anticipation of the biggest MCU film yet: Avengers: Doomsday. Funko Pop has a tempting lineup of Marvel collectibles, including multiple versions of Doctor Doom, beloved X-Men characters, and a 10-inch jumbo Sentinel. Steve Rogers, Thor, Shang-Chi, and several other familiar faces round out the collection.

If your teenager is allowed to watch TV in their room, upgrade their older set to the Mashable Choice Award-winning Hisense DécoTV. The 32-inch model "is compact enough to fit just about anywhere and simplistically chic enough to fit in with just about any decor," said Stodart. It'll be perfect for their college dorm room when the time comes. As a bonus, it costs much less than Samsung's smallest The Frame TV. Read our full review of the Hisense DécoTV.

No one's too old for Play-Doh anymore: This summer, the modeling clay brand released its first-ever collection of adult craft kits, Blooms by Play-Doh. Each one comes with colorful, scented Play-Doh sticks that they can press and shape into a pretty floral bouquet, plus finishing spray and a clear vase. For crafty types who have grown bored of Lego's Botanical builds, this is one of our favorite Christmas gift ideas.

The new Samsung Galaxy Z Flip 8 is the best flip phone we've tested this year, and Mashable's Werth especially recommends it "for a stylish, on-trend young person." It's easy to hold in one hand, durable, and available in an extremely cute purpley-pink color. And while its camera setup isn't wildly impressive, it does take a mean selfie. Read our full review of the Samsung Galaxy Z Flip 8.

Retro tech is having another moment. Last year, cassette players were everywhere; this year, Bluetooth CD players are joining the old-school wave (there are two in this gift guide). They’re a fun pick for Gen Alpha teens who love iPods, disposable cameras, and DVDs, and you can pair it with their favorite artists' latest albums.

The Fosi Audio Merak works as a portable and desktop CD player, with modern extras including Bluetooth, USB drive playback, and one-touch CD ripping.

The best Christmas gift for a hostess with the mostest is a Ninja Slushi Twist. It makes delicious frozen cocktails, slushies, and milkshakes just as well as the original Ninja Slushi, but now it works faster, picks settings for you, and adds a second mixing canister. That's right: Two flavors at once, baby. It's "just plain fun, and will make your home the go-to for your friend group," said Stodart, who gave it a Mashable Choice Award. Read our full review of the Ninja SLUSHi Twist.

Bless the tea sipper in your family with this flavorful collection of 18 premium blends that bring winter warmth and wellness. These loose-leaf teas come in plant-based sachets and are sourced from small-scale farmers. The assortment includes multiple varieties of black, green, mint, oolong, and white teas.

The viral Ninja Crispi and the new Cosori Iconic have both earned the Mashable staff's collective seal of approval. Why those air fryers, you might ask? Not only do they crisp up food nicely, but they're free of plastics and forever chemicals. The compact Crispi is ideal for cooking single-serve meals and meal-prepping; its glass containers come with lids for storing your leftovers. The Cosori is a sleeker stainless steel model with a bigger basket and handy smart controls. Read our full review of the Cosori Iconic.

The new Series 12 is the best smartwatch for most iPhone users, in our opinion. It has a faster processor, pretty new ceramic finish options, and an improved heart sensor array. Mashable senior editor Stan Schroeder has been testing it this fall, and he said the latter is "the star of the show" because it "allows for far more frequent measurements." It also "opens the door for new apps such as Readiness and an overhauled Vitals app," he added.

We loved the Google Fitbit Air when we first tested it, and love it even more after the latest update, which supports automatic detection for up to 100 sports and tracks blood pressure trends. It excels as both a fitness tracker and sleep tracker, making it a superb gift that athletes won’t ever take off. Not to mention it’s way more affordable than the Apple Watch Series 12, Oura Ring 5, and Whoop MG. Read our full review of the Fitbit Air.

Almost everyone on Mashable's shopping team owns an Owala FreeSip, which Mangino dubbed the "best water bottle ever." The 24-ounce insulated stainless steel bottle is designed to accommodate both sipping (via straw) and good ol' fashioned gulp when tipped back. For athletes, college students, teenagers, or anyone who drinks water, we think a colorful Owala is one of the best Christmas gifts under $50. Read our full review of the Owala FreeSip.

Mashable tech reporter Matt Binder, a self-proclaimed "longtime soccer dad," tested the new XbotGo Falcon sports tracking camera for an entire youth soccer season this year. His verdict: It's "a smart pick for parents and coaches." Its footage is sharp, you can monitor it in real time from your smartphone, and it works with nine different sports (soon to be 12). It's a bit of a splurge, but unlike a lot of the competition, it doesn't require a subscription. Read our full review of the XbotGo Falcon.

Tossing the football is a holiday tradition for many sports-loving households. This year, rifle this waterproof football into your dad’s chest. Dime Labs cleverly designed its footballs with silicone grip strips for better handling, and a woven microfiber cover to survive the wettest conditions. It comes in two sizes – 10.5 inches and 8.5 inches – with the smaller version well-suited to kids practicing their quarterback skills.

It's a cooler. It's a boombox. It's both! We love the Igloo KoolTunes for its old-school design and surprisingly good audio quality. While it lacks deep bass, it offers clear, balanced sound and can get quite loud. "It's not a gimmick, but a fun fusion of summer party gear," said Mashable's Henschel. Read our full review of the Igloo KoolTunes.

The new Shark ChillPill is another Mashable Gift of the Year winner. It's a powerful portable fan that stands out for its swappable misting and cooling plate attachments, long battery life, and fun colorways. (Justin Bieber's SKYLRK brand teamed up with Shark for a limited-edition "Heat" variant, which is long sold out.) It came in clutch for Mangino on some of the hottest days of the summer. Read our full review of the Shark ChillPill.

The LifeStraw is a Black Friday classic that always goes on sale around the holidays, which also makes it a perfect stocking stuffer for people who love camping and the great outdoors. You can stick one end of this straw into virtually any water source — no matter how gross — and clean, filtered water comes out the other end.

Portable Bluetooth speakers are crowd-pleasing gifts for just about anyone, from teenagers to parents, siblings, and friends. This year, we're loving the all-new Tribit StormBox Micro 3. It produces satisfying sound in a compact design, is fully waterproof, and comes in multiple standout colorways. Tribit’s speaker is travel-friendly, with a magnetic snap that can latch onto fridge doors or bike handles.

Simply put, Yeti's stainless steel Rambler tumblers are crowd-pleasers. They're dishwasher-safe, incredibly durable, condensation-resistant, and available in a huge rainbow of colors and patterns. Pro tip: For a very affordable personalized Christmas gift, you can customize a Rambler with your own text, graphics, and logos on the Yeti website.

The AirFly Pro is a cult-favorite Bluetooth adapter that makes seatback screens on older planes compatible with wireless headphones. After using it on round-trip flights between Chicago and London, Henschel said she'd "never fly without it again." The newer AirFly Pro 2 has simpler controls, improved sound quality, and pairs faster. Read our full review of the Twelve South AirFly Pro.

Traveling abroad this winter? Take this handy adapter along. Anker’s latest travel charger works with outlets in nearly every country and can charge up to four devices at once. The voltage detection system monitors voltage, power output, and temperature in real time. All readings and charging statuses are displayed on the LCD screen.

Travel jewelry cases are both thoughtful and practical, and we like this one in particular. The velvet box comes in a few different colors, and it ensures your wife, girlfriend, or daughter's favorite rings, necklaces, and earrings never get misplaced when she's away from home. If you're hunting for one of the best Christmas gifts for women under $25, look no further.

Cushy ANC headphones are a non-negotiable for long travel days, and lead shopping reporter Bethany Allard thinks the latest Bose QuietComforts are the best mid-range option for flying. When she wore them on a plane, "I heard minimal engine hum and was able to completely tune out conversations from my fellow passengers," she wrote. "I also never felt the need to remove the headphones due to wear fatigue." Read our full review of the Bose QuietComfort headphones (2nd Gen).

Nori’s garment steamers are a lifesaver for business travelers and fashion professionals. The Cloud Max makes de-wrinkling clothes a breeze, using gentle vacuum suction to pull fabric taut for smoother results. Anti-spit technology prevents leaks and water spots, and the steamer’s portable design fits comfortably in any travel bag.

A weekender bag bridges the gap between a backpack and a suitcase. It should hold a few outfits, toiletries, and an extra pair of shoes for a two- or three-day trip. Quince’s Voyage bag fits the bill with a dedicated shoe compartment, multiple pockets, and a padded shoulder strap. It’s currently on sale for half of its original price, while supplies last.

Tim studied print journalism at the University of Southern California. He currently splits his time between Brooklyn, NY and Charleston, SC. He's currently working on his second novel, a science-fiction book.

#485. Merck tops quarterly estimates, hikes profit outlook as new Keytruda form shows strength

Merck on Thursday topped third-quarter estimates and hiked its adjusted profit outlook, as its immunotherapy Keytruda, including a newer injectable form of the drug, showed stronger-than-expected sales.

The pharmaceutical giant now expects adjusted earnings to be between $2.77 and $2.82 per share. That adjusted profit outlook is up from a previous range of $2.66 to $2.76 per share. The guidance now includes a one-time charge of $400 million, or 12 cents per share, related to its licensing agreement with the Chinese cancer drugmaker SciBrunch.

Merck also narrowed the low end of its 2026 revenue guidance, now expecting sales between $66.8 billion and $67.3 billion. That compares to a previous outlook of $66.3 billion to $67.3 billion.

The company has been on a deal spree as it races to offset generic competition for Keytruda after key patents begin expiring in 2028.

Merck is also positioning the new form of the drug, Keytruda Qlex, as a cornerstone of its growth strategy. The goal is to transition patients from the original intravenous version to Qlex, considered a more convenient under-the-skin injection. This strategy allows the company to defend its market share and sustain Keytruda's blockbuster sales beyond the original version's loss of exclusivity.

Keytruda raked in $8.60 billion in sales for the quarter, beating the $7.73 billion that analysts were expecting, according to StreetAccount. That includes $830 million in sales for Qlex – the highest seen in a quarter since it launched in 2025.

Analysts were expecting $649 million in sales, StreetAccount estimates said. The blowout quarter for the shot suggests it could soon eventually be a multibillion-dollar product annually.

Here's what Merck reported for the third quarter compared with what Wall Street was expecting, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG:

The company posted a net income of $5.07 billion, or $2.04 per share, for the quarter. That compares with net income of $5.79 billion, or $2.32 per share, for the year-earlier period.

Excluding acquisition and restructuring costs, Merck posted earnings of $2.49 per share for the third quarter.

Merck raked in $18.09 billion in revenue for the quarter, up 5% from the same period a year earlier.

Beyond Keytruda, Merck's newer products also showed strong growth.

Winrevair, which is used to treat a rare, deadly lung condition, generated $694 million in sales for the quarter, up 93% from the same period a year earlier. Analysts were expecting sales of $645 million.

Meanwhile, the Gardasil vaccine, which prevents cancers from HPV, a very common sexually transmitted infection, drew about $2 billion in sales due to higher demand in the U.S. That tops the $1.76 billion in sales that analysts were expecting.

That strong revenue comes after Merck last year grappled with elevated Gardasil inventory and weak demand for the vaccine in China.

Meanwhile, Merck's animal health business posted $1.68 billion in sales for the third quarter, which came in slightly below analysts' estimates.

#483. The Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 5x Is Only $900 Right Now

One of my favorite laptops to recommend, the Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 5x, is discounted by $250 to $900. This high-end configuration of the laptop has never been this cheap. That's a pleasant surprise in an industry suffering from an ongoing memory shortage without signs of slowing down.

Just look at these specs: 16 GB of memory, 512 GB of storage, a high-resolution OLED display, and the new Snapdragon X2 Plus. For $900, that's the best Windows laptop deal I've seen in a while. I tested a version with a lower-resolution display (1920 x 1200 rather than 2560 x 1600), and even the quality of that screen impressed me. As it turns out, that model is also being sold for the lowest price I've ever seen it—at Lenovo.com for just $800. Outside of the lower-resolution screen, it has all the same specs.

A year ago, it was fairly common to find excellent laptops for $900. These days, not so much. Increasing memory prices have forced laptop manufacturers to raise their own prices across the board—including Apple. It's become harder than ever to find a high-end laptop under $1,000 that doesn't have any significant compromises. That's an even bigger challenge if you're after a laptop with a larger display. For example, the Dell XPS 13 sells for $900, which is another good option around this price, but it's a tiny device focused on portability. The IdeaPad Slim 5x has a much larger 15.3-inch screen that's great for those who plan to actually sit down at a desk or table and work entirely off it without using an external monitor. At 0.61 inches thick, it's not overly chunky either—matching the thickness of the 14-inch MacBook Pro, for reference.

The chip inside, the Snapdragon X2 Plus, is another reason this laptop deal is so special. This is Qualcomm's latest PC processor, but because of how rocky pricing has been this year, it's rarely shown up in laptops you could call affordable. That's a shame, because it's a very capable processor that's in the same league as Apple's M5 in terms of CPU performance. I wouldn't buy this laptop for full-time video editors or 3D animators—or if you're a serious gamer. The graphics performance just isn't there. But in terms of everyday tasks, whether for office work or schoolwork, the X2 Plus won't skip a beat, no matter how many browser tabs, open applications, and background tasks you have going. It even has plenty of ports onboard, including two USB-C, two USB-A, HDMI, and a microSD card slot.

And last (but not least), the IdeaPad Slim 5x has a touchpad that's nice to use. I mention this because so many budget-oriented laptops cut corners on the quality of the touchpad. That might seem minor, but unless you're a mouse-only person, the touchpad is something you're constantly interacting with and goes a long way toward making a laptop feel premium. The IdeaPad Slim 5x doesn't have a haptic feedback trackpad that more expensive laptops use, so the click is a bit loud. But I can vouch that it doesn't make me feel clumsy when using it.

#480. Eli Lilly hikes sales outlook, as CEO says there's room for 'dramatic' obesity market expansion

Eli Lilly on Thursday reported third-quarter earnings and revenue that blew past estimates and hiked its full-year sales outlook, as demand for its blockbuster weight loss drug Zepbound and diabetes treatment Mounjaro soared again.

Despite that strength, sales of its new GLP-1 obesity pill Foundayo, which launched in the U.S. in April, were under Wall Street's expectations for the quarter.

The pharmaceutical giant now expects 2026 revenue to come in between $91 billion and $92 billion, up from a previous guidance of $85 billion to $87 billion.

Lilly projects its full-year adjusted earnings will be between $35 and $36 per share, which compares with a previous outlook of $35.50 to $36.50 per share. The company said it raised the underlying profit guidance by $4.07 per share at the midpoint, but noted that it is offset by $4.57 per share in charges tied to deals in the quarter.

The company's shares rose about 7% on Thursday.

Lilly's massive diabetes and obesity windfall – and market share lead over chief rival Novo – shows no signs of slowing down, even as the company grapples with lower net prices in the U.S. The pharma giant is converting its massive profits into a deal-making spree, most recently striking an agreement to buy Merida Biosciences to develop a new class of treatments for serious autoimmune and allergic diseases.

Here's what Eli Lilly reported for the third quarter compared with what Wall Street was expecting, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG:

Resilient demand for Zepbound and Mounjaro has helped fuel several strong quarters for Lilly despite lower prices for the medications in the U.S., which came after a drug pricing deal struck with the Trump administration last year. In a release, Lilly also pointed to expanded U.S. coverage for obesity care, referring to Medicare's decision to start covering GLP-1s for weight loss in July under a temporary pilot program.

"This is a program that's really working," Lilly CEO Dave Ricks said on CNBC's "Squawk on the Street." "We're pleased with the early uptake and access, and I think doctors and patients are as well."

Mounjaro's worldwide revenue rose 65% to $10.72 billion for the quarter, including U.S. sales of about $5 billion. That surpassed the $10.10 billion in worldwide sales and $4.79 billion in U.S. revenue that analysts were expecting for the quarter, according to StreetAccount.

Mounjaro notably saw strength internationally, with sales outside the U.S. jumping 93%.

Zepbound, which entered the market roughly three years ago, posted $5.35 billion in revenue for the third quarter. That's up 49% from the year-earlier period, as demand for the drug also rose while realized prices dropped. The vast majority of those sales came from the U.S.

Analysts were expecting $5.09 billion in global sales for Zepbound, including $4.99 billion from the U.S., according to StreetAccount.

Lilly's newly launched obesity pill, Foundayo, which won U.S. approval in April, took in $184 million in sales for the third quarter. That fell under analyst forecasts of around $229 million in sales, StreetAccount estimates showed.

It marks the second earnings report that includes revenue from the GLP-1 pill, which is competing head-to-head with a rival oral drug from Novo that launched in January.

Total U.S. prescriptions for Foundayo and the number of new Foundayo patients in the third quarter doubled from the previous quarter, Lilly CFO Lucas Montarces said during a Thursday earnings call. Around 4 in 10 patients starting an oral obesity medicine choose Foundayo, he added.

Lilly expects Foundayo to win U.S. approval for Type 2 diabetes in the fourth quarter.

Lilly is working to maintain its dominance in the booming market for GLP-1 drugs, with the company holding 63% share of the U.S. obesity and diabetes drug market in the third quarter, according to an earnings presentation on Thursday. Novo's market share in the quarter was 36.6%.

During the earnings call, Montarces said 7 out of 10 U.S. prescriptions for injectable obesity and diabetes drugs in the third quarter were for a Lilly medicine.

Ricks told CNBC that he estimates 3% to 10% of eligible patients access obesity care in the U.S., but said the "room for expansion here of this market is dramatic." Lilly is at the front of that push, he added.

Internationally, Lilly held 58.4% share of the market, while Novo had 41.6%, the presentation said.

Eli Lilly's revenue in the U.S. climbed 34% to $15.1 billion. Lilly said it saw a 41% increase in volume — or the number of prescriptions or units sold — for its products, primarily for Mounjaro and Zepbound. That was partially offset by a 7% decrease in realized prices, primarily driven by Zepbound.

Lilly's quarter was also boosted by a sales-based milestone payout of $410 million for its Type 2 diabetes medication Jardiance, related to the company's collaboration with Boehringer Ingelheim.

Sales outside the U.S. jumped 47% to $9.3 billion, propelled by a 76% surge in volume and partly offset by a 29% drop in realized prices.

The pharmaceutical giant booked net income of $6.45 billion, or $7.22 per share, for the third quarter, which includes the $4.57 per share deal charges. That compares with net income of $5.58 billion, or $6.21 per share, a year earlier.

Excluding one-time items associated with the value of intangible assets and other adjustments, Eli Lilly posted earnings of $7.48 per share for the third quarter.

#478. Democrats Sweep Republicans in Nearly Every Race That Matters

Democrats stormed through key battleground races across the US in their battle to capture the House and Senate on Tuesday night, marking a decisive repudiation of President Donald Trump’s second term.

The scale of victory for Democrats—in some races, the party flipped seats that Trump won by double digits just two years ago—marked a historic night that exceeded the party’s highest expectations.

Democrats pulled off arguably the greatest upset in Texas, where James Talarico defeated scandal-plagued Republican state attorney general Ken Paxton and where Gina Hinojosa defeated Greg Abbott for the governorship, despite the millions and millions of dollars spent by billionaire Elon Musk on behalf of the Republicans. No Democrat had won a statewide seat election since 1994.

Democrats also seized other critical Senate races on election night, including in Kansas, South Carolina, Iowa, and North Carolina, while retaining control of seats in Georgia and New Hampshire, according to the Associated Press.

At the White House, stunned Trump officials tell WIRED that high gas prices and the increased cost of living brought on by the Iran war were the principal reasons for widespread GOP losses.

“If any good comes out of tonight for the Republican party, it’s that no Republican president will ever listen to imbeciles like Mark Levin and Marc Thiessen again,” one source close to the White House said of two commentators who had urged Trump to prolong the Iran war.

Exit polling showing massive defections from other parts of the 2024 Trump coalition show there was more to the losses than that, with Latino voters turning to Democrats as the administration pursued brutal and unpopular immigration policies.

Some officials, who were granted anonymity to speak candidly, privately laid the blame at the feet of the president for taking the nation into the Middle East conflict, which he wrongly assumed would be over in a matter of weeks and has continued with no clear end in sight.

“President Trump was not on the ballot, and it’s proven that Trump voters show up when he is on the ballot,” a White House official said in a statement, even as Trump had implored his base on the trail to pretend that he was on the ballot.

“Also, candidate quality matters, and President Trump did a better job promoting many of the candidates on the ballot than the candidates did themselves,” the official added.

Many of the losing candidates were hand-picked by Trump, who forced out incumbents like Texas senator John Cornyn and blessed candidates like Darline Graham (sister of late senator Lindsey Graham), who ran a dismal campaign in South Carolina.

Still, other Trump officials have cast about for other scapegoats, blaming a failed redistricting effort as well as candidate quality.

Republicans embarked on a strategy earlier this year to redraw numerous congressional maps as part of a gambit that White House aides thought could yield 10 to 15 House seat pickups if Trump voters turned out. The downside, political scientists pointed out, was that it made seats harder to defend, as while there were more Republican districts, each was less Republican.

On election night, the strategy failed to yield results. Democrats won at least three House seats in Florida that Republicans had redrawn, as well as the seat in North Carolina.

The closest thing to a bright spot for Republicans came in the Senate race in Florida, which became abruptly competitive in the final days of the midterm campaign. In the end, Ashley Moody barely fended off the progressive candidate, Democrat Angie Nixon.

As the likely control of the House and Senate became clear, top House Democrats separately ended the night relishing the prospect of mounting an aggressive oversight campaign against the Trump administration.

Robert Garcia, the incoming chair of the House Oversight Committee, issued a two-word statement: “Lawyer up.”

#471. Review: I have no complaints about the Fitbit Edge, but I prefer the Fitbit Air

After careful hands-on testing, we feature our favorite gear and gadgets as Mashable Selects products in our dedicated shopping guides.

The fitness tracker world is crowded, and researching the best model is now a major task. If you're not looking to spend a ton of money, Google has a new Fitbit that might be perfect.

The Fitbit Edge feels rightfully placed between the minimalist Fitbit Air and the Pixel Watch 5. Not only does the $179.99 price fit in the middle of the two, but its functions land somewhere in the middle. It adds elements missing on the Fitbit Air like onboard GPS and an altimeter. But it lacks features you’ll find on the Pixel Watch 5, like Google Wallet for contactless payments.

I’ve been wearing the Fitbit Edge for the last few weeks, testing out its comfort and functions. While it has tons of features that will be great for some people, I’m still more excited about the Fitbit Air compared to the Edge.

Google has gone back to a screen with the Fitbit Edge after giving us the faceless Fitbit Air. The Edge’s display is still quite small when compared to most Garmins or an Apple Watch, but it packs in features.

The Google Health Coach is one of my favorite aspects about the Fitbit lineup. It takes just a few minutes to come up with a detailed fitness plan. The “coach” checks in, but not in a badgering way. Instead, I find the reminders helpful to get a snapshot of what type of movement would be best based on other metrics like sleep and heart rate.

Nutrition tracking is also a main feature with Google’s Fitbit platform. You can scan barcodes into the app or even take photos of food to enter it into your daily intake.

Function aside, I like the looks of the Fitbit Edge. It’s simple, sleek, and doesn’t look massive on my wrist. Google ships the Edge with a silicone Active Band in two sizes. I’ve found this to be the most comfortable option from the few I’ve tested. The best tech deal this week The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile

The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile

I also like the Magnet Band, but I found it fiddly to get the right fit. For a fancier look, the Metal Links Band looks snazzy. The $149.99 price, however, is kind of scary considering the Edge itself doesn’t cost much more. I haven’t tested it, but I suspect my favorite band would be the Performance Loop Band since that’s my preferred option on the Fitbit Air. But the point stands that Google has plentiful options for bands that make the tracker feel more customized to your liking.

Like the Fitbit Air, the Edge is beyond impressive when it comes to battery life. I’ve been getting about a week of wear before I need to recharge. When it does need a recharge, it takes less than 90 minutes to top out at 100 percent. I also found Google’s claim to be true that a five-minute recharge earns you about a day of battery life.

Compare that to the Apple Watch 11, which Mashable Senior Editor Stan Schroeder found to get about 24 hours on one charge when testing, and there’s a clear winner. If you value long battery life, you’re better off with the Fitbit Edge.

On top of the battery life, Google has made the Edge with a replaceable battery, a first for the brand. Should the battery crap out in a handful of years, pop a new one in, and you’ll be back to new.

Up until the Fitbit Edge arrived on my doorstep, I had been wearing the Fitbit Air for over four months almost 24/7. The Air remains the most comfortable fitness tracker I’ve ever worn. I wouldn't consider the Edge to be uncomfortable, but it doesn’t go unnoticed on the wrist like the Air. After a week or so, I got more accustomed to the feel of the Edge and noticed it less often, but it doesn’t disappear like the Air does.

Pair this slightly less comfortable fit with the new Fitbit Air Metal Mesh Band that I love, and I’m still more excited about the Air compared to the Edge. I should mention I have petite wrists, so your comfort with the Edge will vary.

The Fitbit Edge is perfect for those who want an uncomplicated fitness tracker that doesn’t come with a shocking price tag. It has great fitness tracking metrics and impressive sleep monitoring. It’s also pretty comfortable on the wrist, and the week-long battery life is a major benefit.

If you’re looking for something without a watch face or you want to barely notice you’re wearing a fitness tracker, I think the Fitbit Air is a better option. However, if you want a watch face to glance at the time or you like to track stairs climbed, you’ll want the Fitbit Edge. On the flip side, if you’re looking for a fully functional smartwatch and fitness tracker in one device, I think the Pixel Watch 5 wins over the Fitbit Edge.

#467. Cruise companies aim to keep fuel costs down. Their strategies for doing so differ

Carnival, Royal Caribbean and Norwegian Cruise Line Holdings posted strong earnings for their most recent quarters despite rising fuel prices. How the leading cruise companies navigate fuel costs boils down to starkly different strategies.

Oil prices have skyrocketed since the U.S.-Israel war with Iran began on Feb. 28. Brent crude oil reached a six-month high on Friday, settling at $116.72 per barrel. With no clear end in sight for the conflict in the Middle East, the pressure affecting cruise ships' lifeblood seems poised to last into the holiday travel season and beyond.

Both Royal Caribbean and Norwegian practice "hedging," or a strategy of using derivatives to reduce exposure to swings in the price of fuel, to account for sharp increases.

Carnival CEO Josh Weinstein, on the other hand, told CNBC in an interview last month that cutting fuel consumption is the best way to avert the effects of expensive fuel.

"At the end of the day, fuel is an input cost for us. The best thing that we can do to control that cost is to use less," Weinstein said at the time.

Jefferies analyst David Katz told CNBC in an interview that companies that hedge do so primarily to manage the cost of fuel, but also to manage Wall Street expectations and prevent hectic stock trading based on fluctuations in the price of fuel.

"When you're public, the Street will trade your stock around based on the price of fuel," Katz said. "The Street's argument is that volatility puts pressure on your multiple."

"While it is mathematically most likely true that over the long term it is more expensive," he explained. "The benefit of having less fuel volatility in the model and less trading volatility is [it's] good for your multiple."

Despite the potential positives of the strategy, Carnival has maintained the stance it has held since 2019: Cutting fuel consumption works better than hedging.

And Carnival's third-quarter earnings report last month suggests the strategy may be paying off.

Carnival beat analysts' expectations on both the top and bottom lines for its most recent quarter and reported an all-time high net income of $1.9 billion.

Weinstein told CNBC in an interview on "Squawk on the Street" following the release that the company has been "maniacal" about cutting its fuel consumption, saying it's slashed its unit fuel consumption rate by 26% since 2019.

"We estimate we've saved about $700 million in 2026 based on that consumption savings rate going down since 2019," he said.

Carnival spent $615 million, or about 7.3% of its revenue, on fuel in the third quarter, according to its most recent earnings release. That's an increase from the $425 million, or 6.7% of revenue, that the company spent on fuel in the fourth quarter of 2025, before fuel prices spiked.

Carnival projects its fuel costs will rise to $640 million in the fourth quarter, according to its earnings release.

Royal Caribbean similarly beat analyst expectations for earnings per share for its third quarter, reported Tuesday. However, it narrowly missed on revenue.

CEO Jason Liberty attributed the company's beat in part to its hedging strategy during an interview on CNBC's "Squawk on the Street" Tuesday morning.

"We're a little bit over 60% hedged here for 2026, and so that's helping insulate us from some of the impacts on the rising fuel costs," he said.

"It's obviously still impacting us," Liberty said. "[High fuel prices] evaporated a good chunk of our Q3 earnings beat into the full-year guide. But we're continuing to hedge, and we watch."

Royal Caribbean spent about $347 million on fuel in the third quarter, or about 6.2% of its revenue, according to its earnings release. That compares with $293 million, or 6.8% of revenue, spent on fuel in the fourth quarter of 2025, which ended on Dec. 31.

The company projects fuel costs will continue to rise to $379 million in the fourth quarter.

Liberty pointed out that high fuel prices have not dampened demand from consumers for vacations.

"It's not that we don't see points of challenges, but really what we've seen is that even in those points of challenges, the consumer comes roaring back," he said.

Royal Caribbean reported strong bookings for the third quarter and said reservations for 2027 are already up by a high-teens percentage.

Norwegian Cruise Line Holdings beat on both the top and bottom lines for its third-quarter earnings, reported on Thursday, with revenue of $2.9 billion and adjusted earnings per share of $1.12.

The company has hedged approximately 48% of its fuel consumption for 2026, according to the earnings release.

Norwegian spent about $196 million on fuel in the third quarter, or about 6.6% of its revenue, according to its most recent earnings release. That's a lower share of revenue than the 7.4% — totaling $167 million — spent on fuel in the fourth quarter of 2025, which ended on Dec. 31.

The company projects fuel consumption to rise slightly in the fourth quarter, up to 255,000 metric tons from 239,000 metric tons consumed in the third quarter.

The company is in the midst of a turnaround effort. And despite facing added challenges from the macro environment, Chief Financial Officer Mark Kempa said he is reassured by this quarter's results on an earnings call on Thursday.

"These results reinforce our confidence in the appeal of our products and the opportunity to translate stronger revenue performance and disciplined cost management into improved profitability," Kempa said.

#456. Rivian third-quarter earnings beat estimates as software revenue, R2 deliveries rise

Rivian Automotive beat Wall Street's third-quarter earnings expectations as it ramped up production of its new R2 entry-level SUV that the company has promised investors will lead it to profitability.

Here's how Rivian performed in the period ended Sept. 30, compared with average estimates compiled by LSEG:

Shares of Rivian were up roughly 7% during afterhours trading Thursday, after hitting a new 52-week low of $11.38 earlier in the day. The stock closed at $11.45 a share, down 1.9%

The electric vehicle maker also revised its 2026 guidance to mark expected improvements in its vehicle deliveries, pre-tax adjusted earnings and capital expenditures.

The new guidance calls for a pre-tax adjusted loss of between $1.75 billion and $1.85 billion — a $100 million improvement at the midpoint from its prior guidance — vehicle deliveries of between 67,000 and 70,000 units, up from at least 65,000; and capital expenditures of between $1.4 billion and $1.5 billion, $300 million less at the midpoint.

Rivian attributed the improvement in its pre-tax adjusted earnings guidance to better-than-expected revenue related to its sales of regulatory credits, an IEEPA tariff refund receivable in the third quarter and its expected increase in vehicle deliveries.

The R2 — the first deliveries of which arrived to customers in June — has become Rivian's best-selling model and was responsible for "much of the gain quarter-over-quarter," the company said.

Rivian delivered a record 19,248 units from July through September. The company does not disclose deliveries by vehicle.

The EV maker remains unprofitable overall but continued to narrow its losses during the quarter. The company reported a net loss attributable to common stockholders of $913 million, compared with a loss of $1.17 billion during the third quarter of 2025.

Rivian's gross profit, which is closely monitored by investors, was $176 million during the third quarter, up from $24 million a year earlier. Its adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization was a loss of $435 million, a $167 million improvement from the same period last year.

The company reported that its software and services segment continues to grow, generating $605 million in revenue and a gross profit of $256 million, a 42% margin. That compares to its automotive operations, which recorded nearly $1.55 billion in revenue and a gross loss of $80 million.

Also on Thursday, Rivian reiterated that it expects the R2, a smaller and less expensive sibling to its current luxury R1S SUV, to have a positive gross margin by the end of the year. CEO RJ Scaringe has said the company needs to scale beyond current R2 production plans of 160,000 units in order to achieve overall profitability.

"That ramp-up is critical for us getting to positive gross margin on R2 and that ultimately will contribute to positive gross margin for the business," Scaringe told CNBC's Phil LeBeau during an interview Thursday. "We're going to see that through the end of the quarter and the unit economics will continue to grow … into Q1 of next year as well."

Rivian on Thursday said its cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments balance was $5.5 billion, up from $5.3 billion to end the second quarter.

#452. Starbucks sales miss expectations, but its U.S. turnaround is gaining steam

Starbucks on Thursday reported mixed quarterly results as its international cafes underperformed expectations.

However, its U.S. turnaround continues to take hold, as its home market topped expectations during the coffee giant's final quarter of fiscal 2026.

"We enter fiscal 2027 with momentum, a clear set of priorities and higher ambitions for what Starbucks can become," CEO Brian Niccol said in a video shared on the company's website.

Starbucks is ahead of schedule to meet the fiscal 2028 targets laid out at its investor day in January, he said on the company's earnings conference call.

For fiscal 2027, Starbucks is projecting adjusted earnings per share in a range of $3.15 to $3.25, above Wall Street's expectations of earnings per share of $3.14. However, its anticipated revenue decline of 1% is weaker than expected; analysts were forecasting net sales growth of 1.4%.

Starbucks is projecting North American same-store sales growth of 4% for the fiscal year.

The company's earnings and revenue outlook includes an additional week and the effects of the shift in its China business to a joint venture business model. Starbucks is also projecting slight deflation in coffee prices and slowing net new North American cafe openings, which will both weigh on its full-year revenue, according to CFO Cathy Smith.

Here's what the company reported for the quarter ended Sept. 27 compared with what Wall Street was expecting, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG:

Starbucks reported fiscal fourth-quarter net income attributable to the company of $677.2 million, or 59 cents per share, up from $133.1 million, or 12 cents per share, a year earlier.

Excluding restructuring and impairment costs and other items, the company reported earnings per share of 80 cents.

Net revenue fell 4% to $9.14 billion, reflecting the joint venture deal in China.

The company's global same-store sales increased 7.2%, fueled by growth in average ticket, and beating Wall Street estimates of 6%, according to StreetAccount. Transactions grew 1.8% in the quarter.

Starbucks' U.S. cafes reported same-store sales growth of 7.7%, topping StreetAccount estimates of a 6.5% increase.

Under Niccol's "Back to Starbucks" strategy, the company has focused on improving service, making its cafes more welcoming and sharpening its marketing. The changes have helped to win back customers.

"Starbucks brand affinity is at near record levels as our menu innovation, marketing and merchandise continue to create moments that drive culture and bring people into our coffee houses," Niccol told analysts.

The company said its North American rollout of its fall menu, which includes the iconic pumpkin spice latte, was the company's strongest ever autumn launch day. And matcha is now a $1 billion drink for Starbucks.

Outside of North America, the company's international comparable sales ticked up 0.9%, as traffic declines offset an increase to average ticket. That growth fell short of analyst estimates of a 3.2% increase, according to StreetAccount.

After its China business transitioned to a joint venture, Starbucks has shifted most of its international business to a licensed model, allowing local operators to take charge. The company is also exploring selling a majority stake in its Japan business, Reuters reported in September.

Starbucks opened 303 net new cafes during the quarter. In September, the company announced it would close about 1% of its North American footprint, or about 250 locations, as part of its turnaround.

By the end of its fiscal year, across the U.S. and Canada, the company also completed more than 1,700 cafe uplifts, meant to make its stores more welcoming to customers. The company has said locations that receive a makeover, with tweaks like increased seating and softer lighting, see higher transactions in the aftermath.
